Lemma
[distance via constant-speed curves]

Source: petersen:page-0198 ↗ def:pet-ch5-distance ↗ cor:pet-ch5-regular-curve-approx

Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian manifold and $p,q\in M$. Then \[ |pq|=\inf \{ L(\gamma )\mid \gamma \in \Omega _{p,q}\text{ of constant speed}\} , \] i.e. the infimum defining the Riemannian distance is unchanged if the competing curves are required to have constant speed. (When $p$ and $q$ lie in different components both infima are over the empty set, and the identity is the degenerate one carried by the convention for $|pq|$ in that case; no connectedness hypothesis is needed.)
Proof

↗ cor:pet-ch5-regular-curve-approx \sketch Restricting the competitor class can only increase the infimum. Conversely, section 3 replaces any $c\in \Omega _{p,q}$ by a constant-speed $\bar c$ with $L(\bar c)\le (1+\epsilon )L(c)$. Let $\epsilon \downarrow 0$ and then infimize over $c$. Both classes are empty simultaneously when the endpoints lie in different components.

□
